thread:
maria: Heads up — seeing a slot-jam in us-west2-a that’s been blocking tiny GPU jobs for ~45m. small pods Pending.

aj: seen it. is it the warmpool? nodes appear healthy but not scheduling.

maria: looks like node label mismatch: warmpool nodes are labeled gpu-type=a100 but the autoscaler recently provisioned an rtx pool. tiny-pod nodeSelector is gpu-type=a100 so scheduler refuses rtx.

leo: can you paste the pod/nodes snippet?

maria: ```
$ kubectl get pods -n ml -o wide | grep Pending
train-abc123    0/1 Pending   0  2h  --> nodeSelector: gpu-type=a100
inference-small 0/1 Pending  0  10m --> nodeSelector: gpu-type=a100
```

yun: infra-bot: any autoscaler events around scale up?

infra-bot: autoscaler/us-west2-a scaled up 2 nodes (nodepool: rp-rtx-mix) at 2026-03-23T14:05:33Z — created nodes with labels: gpu-type=rtx

aj: so autoscaler created rtx nodes but scheduler won't place a100-constrained pods. that leaves tiny free fragments on a100 nodes but not contiguous slots for gang/bigger pods.

leo: classic fragmentation + mixed-shape pools. options: 1) make autoscaler prefer a100 pool for pending pods with nodeSelector 2) relax pod selectors 3) evict low-priority batch on a100 to compact.

maria: my fav short-term: update cluster-autoscaler scaleUpFromZero/expander rules to prefer nodepool with label gpu-type=a100 when pending pods include nodeSelector gpu-type=a100. and bump warmpool min for the a100 pool by +1.

yun: cost hit? a100 reserved are pricier. but these jobs are prod-critical. if we keep increasing warmpool for a100 we pay more idle cost. need tradeoff doc.

aj: quick mitigation idea: run a planned drain on one low-util a100 node to force defragmentation (drain low-priority pods only). frees contiguous slots. less risky than wide defrag.

leo: agree. cordon+drain but only evict pods with priority!=high. runbook checklist?

maria: runbook ready. command I’ll run after thumbs up: ```
kubectl cordon node/us-west2-a100-07 && kubectl drain node/us-west2-a100-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --pod-selector='!priority=high'
```

infra-bot: scheduled maintenance window for drain at 2026-03-23T14:20Z (notifying on-call).

leo: monitoring — if latency spikes > 200ms or 5xxs, ping me.

maria: started drain now.

[6m later]

maria: update: pending 2 -> 0, scheduler placed 3 small pods onto freed node. defrag helped.

yun: follow-ups: 1) add autoscaler preference rule (prefer a100 nodepool when pending includes nodeSelector gpu-type=a100) 2) warmpool +1 for a100 3) alert when pending gpu pods >5 for >10m 4) doc cost vs availability tradeoff for reserved a100 buffer.

aj: filing PR for autoscaler config change, assigning to @yun and @maria for review. :thumbsup: 

maria: thanks. leaving this thread for follow-up on cost tradeoffs and PR.
